title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, agent-node behaviour, billing qualifications and control paths are supported by the sources checked. The allocation API is documented despite the automatic pre-check warning; searches found no documented switch dedicated to the node or automation for its human-assistance setting.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes environment credit allocations and tenant-pool enforcement rules.

claims.claim: MCSMessages is the Copilot Credits entitlement ID used in allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID MCSMessages and are managed through the licensing/allocationsV2 operations of the Power Platform API.

claims.claim: The allocation.quantity property sets the number of allocated credits.
claims.quote: allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages" allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } enforcementRules = @( @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ) } )

claims.claim: An enforcementRules entry with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false stops tenant-pool draw.
claims.quote: Disable TenantPool so the environment is capped at its allocation. Set enabled = $true to let the environment draw from tenant capacity. @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.claim: A published environment-group tenant-draw rule makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override a published environment-group tenant-draw rule.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment. Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Allowing or disallowing tooling and MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not yet be available in every region.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents within their policy scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope. To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies govern certified connectors.
claims.quote: Certified connectors | Supported | First-party and certified third-party connectors. Full allow/block at the connector and action level.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies support MCP server-level governance.
claims.quote: MCP connectors | Supported | MCP server-level blocking is available. Within advanced connector policies, administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom connectors are not yet supported by ACP and are governed using classic data policies.
claims.quote: Custom connectors | Not yet supported | Planned as a separate rule type in a future release. Use classic data policies for custom connector governance.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: HTTP connectors are not yet supported by ACP and are governed using classic data policies.
claims.quote: HTTP connectors | Not yet supported | Planned alongside custom connector support. Use classic data policies and connector endpoint filtering for HTTP governance.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Classic data policies are ignored in ACP-only mode.
claims.quote: ACP-only mode: Classic data policies are ignored for the scope, and ACP is the only connector policy that's evaluated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Scopes depending on classic data policies for custom or HTTP connector governance must retain mixed mode.
claims.quote: Don't rely on a data policy for any control in an ACP-only scope, including custom connectors, HTTP connectors, endpoint filtering, and virtual connectors. If a scope still depends on data policies, keep it in mixed mode.

claims.claim: ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out to Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order: 1. Power Automate maker portal — rolling out first 2. Copilot Studio — following Power Automate 3. Power Apps maker portal — following Copilot Studio

claims.claim: Until design-time enforcement is available for Copilot Studio, ACP enforcement for that workload is runtime-only.
claims.quote: Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP's policy layer evaluates each MCP tool request.

claims.claim: Existing Copilot Studio and environment authoring permissions control who can build in an environment.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot harness doesn't have its own maker-access setting. To control who can create agents, use your existing Copilot Studio and environment permissions.
